inlineCode: // Pass 1: every Active Actor Wolf stays a Wolf for the rest of the match.
// Outside WOLF MODE it stalks while disguised as a white Human; after cooldown
// it re-enters WOLF MODE, chases, freezes one Human, cools down, and repeats.
const actualMove = Math.hypot(wx - prevActualX, wy - prevActualY);
const blocked = actualMove < Math.max(0.35, lastExpectedMove * aiWolfBlockedRatio);
wolf.__iceWolfAIWolfBlockedFor = blocked ? blockedFor + dt : Math.max(0, blockedFor - dt * 2);
const forceDiagnosticPlayerTarget = wolf.__iceWolfDiagnosticTargetPlayer === true && diagPhase === 1 && pRole === 'Human' && pState === 'Active';
const d = Math.hypot(human.getCenterXInScene() - wx, human.getCenterYInScene() - wy);
if (d < targetDist) { target = human; targetDist = d; }
const diagnosticPlayerFreeze = wolf.__iceWolfDiagnosticTargetPlayer === true && vars.get('CpuWolfDiagPhase').getAsNumber() === 1 && target === player;
// Hidden stalking: the awakened Wolf remains visually white outside
// WOLF MODE, but keeps closing the distance instead of wandering away.
wolf.setX(Math.max(-708, Math.min(692, wolf.getX() + vx * speed * dt)));
wolf.setY(Math.max(-708, Math.min(692, wolf.getY() + vy * speed * dt)));
const d = Math.hypot(px - x, py - y);
if (d < best) { best = d; threat = { x: px, y: py, dist: d }; }
const d = Math.hypot(cx - x, cy - y);
if (d < best) { best = d; threat = { x: cx, y: cy, dist: d }; }
// Pass 2: Human wander/flee/rescue AI. Any visible Wolf (Player or awakened
// Actor Wolf) is treated as a threat only while that Wolf is in WOLF MODE.
const humanActualMove = Math.hypot(ax - humanPrevActualX, ay - humanPrevActualY);
const humanBlocked = humanActualMove < Math.max(0.35, humanLastExpectedMove * humanBlockedRatio);
actor.__iceWolfAIHumanBlockedFor = humanBlocked ? humanBlockedFor + dt : Math.max(0, humanBlockedFor - dt * 2);
const pd = Math.hypot(px - ax, py - ay);
const td = Math.hypot(tx - ax, ty - ay);
if (td < rescueTargetDist && td <= rescueSearchRadius) { rescueTarget = target; rescueTargetDist = td; }
actor.setX(Math.max(-708, Math.min(692, actor.getX() + vx * speed * dt)));
actor.setY(Math.max(-708, Math.min(692, actor.getY() + vy * speed * dt)));

eventsFunctionsExtensions.name: SpriteMultitouchJoystick
description: Multitouch joysticks are objects showing a joystick on the screen, useful for mobile. They work like a physical gamepad:

- Automatic "mapper" behaviors for 2D and 3D movement behaviors (platformer characters, top-down movement, 3D character etc...). Add one of these to the object with the movement behavior (i.e: the player most of the time) and the behavior will then be controlled automatically by the virtual joystick (it works by reading the multitouch joystick state and simulating controls). No need for additional events to make it work once the behaviors are set up.
There are ready-to-use joysticks in the asset-store [multitouch joysticks pack](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?initial-dialog=asset-store&asset-pack=multitouch-joysticks-multitouch-joysticks).

events.comment:
At each frame, the camera must catchup the target by a given ratio (speed)
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1) - targetX) * (1 - speed)

The frame rate must not impact on the catch-up speed, we don't want a speed in ratio per frame but a speed ratio per second, like this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1s) - targetX) * (1 - speed)

Ok, but we still need to process each frame, we can use a exponent for this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * (1 - speed)^timeDelta
cameraX(t) = targetX + (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * exp(timeDelta * ln((1 - speed)))

pow is probably more efficient than precalculated log if the speed is changed continuously but this might be rare enough.

parameters: TargetedRotationAngle + 90 + RotationAngleOffset + AngleDifference(CameraAngle(Object.Layer()), TargetedRotationAngle + 90 + RotationAngleOffset) * exp(TimeDelta() * RotationLogSpeed)
TargetedElevationAngle + ElevationAngleOffset + AngleDifference(90 - Scene3D::CameraRotationX(Object.Layer()), TargetedElevationAngle + ElevationAngleOffset) * exp(TimeDelta() * ElevationLogSpeed)
